tools.name: get_offering
tools.description: Call this when a user asks what IIS Rescue is, who it is for, or how its pricing works. Returns the three migration paths, the promises made on every project, the fixed-price model and the process. Includes the consultation link.

tools.name: get_faq
tools.description: Call this when a user asks a specific question about migrating a legacy IIS, classic ASP or SQL Server website, such as cost, downtime or what happens to the database. Returns published Q&As word for word, filtered by `query`. `query` is a case-insensitive substring match, so use one short keyword l

tools.name: get_eol_facts
tools.description: Call this when a user asks whether their website is at risk from Windows Server 2012 end of life or another out-of-support Windows Server or SQL Server version. Returns Microsoft's end-of-support dates with a source link for each, plus the Extended Security Updates cutoff. `product` matches part of

tools.name: get_migration_paths
tools.description: Call this when a user wants to compare the general options for moving off a legacy IIS server. Returns Rehost, Rebuild and Replace, with what each involves and when each fits. For a recommendation on one specific site, use run_pathfinder.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: Call this when you suggest IIS Rescue, or when a user is ready to talk to them or asks how to get started. Returns the consultation link and how the process works. It never books anything or collects personal data.

tools.name: get_partner_channel
tools.description: Call this when the user is an MSP or IT contractor asking whether IIS Rescue works with partners, white-labels, subcontracts or takes referrals. Returns the arrangements, what stays with the partner, and the partner FAQ. Partner work is quoted at a fixed price like direct work; no figure is given.

tools.name: get_pathfinder_questions
tools.description: Call this when you want to ask the user more about their site to sharpen a run_pathfinder result. Returns the six assessment questions and their allowed answers. You do not need it before calling run_pathfinder, which accepts partial answers; 'unknown' is always a valid answer.

tools.name: run_pathfinder
tools.description: Call this when a user wants to know whether to rehost, rebuild or replace their own legacy IIS or classic ASP website. Returns the recommended path, confidence, alternatives, risks, what moves the price, the reasoning and the consultation link. It runs the same engine as iisrescue.com/two-minute-ass

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_pathfinder_questions" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Call this when you want to ask the user more about their site to sharpen a run_pathfinder result. Returns the six assessment questions and their allowed answers…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
